verdict.rationale: AMD's first-party GAIA framework runs AI agents locally by default on Ryzen AI hardware and says local inference keeps user data private and supports air-gapped deployment. Data that never leaves the device can't be harvested for cloud training. This is an inferred outcome of on-device execution rather than an explicit no-training commitment, so it earns only partial credit. Missing for 10: an explicit AMD statement or policy that user data is not used for model training, guarantees covering the broader Ryzen AI software stack beyond GAIA, and independent or hands-on corroboration of no data egress.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Local inference keeps your data private, avoids cloud usage fees, and supports air-gapped deployment with hardware-accelerated performance.
GAIA is AMD's open-source framework for building intelligent AI agents that run locally by default on AMD Ryzen AI hardware.
